theme: What a loud alarm does to the first hours of your morning, and how light and a steady schedule do the same job more gently.

grammar.point_en: as soon as A, then B
grammar.structure: subject + 一 + verb 1 + (subject 2) + 就 + verb 2
grammar.explain_en: 一……就…… marks two things happening immediately one after the other: as soon as the first action happens, the second follows. 一 sits directly in front of the first verb; 就 comes before the second verb, after the second subject when the two subjects differ (他一说，我就明白了). The same frame also describes a standing habit — whenever A happens, B always follows (他一喝酒脸就红) — and a reaction you cannot control (一说到考试，我就紧张). When both clauses share one subject, put the subject at the front and keep 一 next to the verb: 我一进门就看见他, not 一我一进门就……. Compare 刚……就……, which reports a past sequence where the first action had only just finished, so it is tied to a single moment; 一……就…… is not tied to the past and is the natural choice for rules, habits and general statements. Compare 如果……就……, which leaves the first event as a possibility instead of presenting it as immediate.
grammar.common_mistake: A common error is to slide a time word between 一 and the verb: 我一昨天就见过他. 一 must touch the verb itself, so the time word moves outside the frame. Learners also write 才 in the second clause, which reverses the immediacy the pattern is built on.

examples.zh: 他一进门就发现气氛不对。
examples.py: tā yí jìn mén jiù fā xiàn qì fēn bú duì
examples.en: The moment he came in, he sensed that the mood was wrong.

examples.zh: 铃声一响，我就坐了起来。
examples.py: líng shēng yì xiǎng wǒ jiù zuò le qǐ lái
examples.en: As soon as the bell rang, I sat up.

examples.zh: 这个孩子一看见水就不肯走。
examples.py: zhè ge hái zi yí kàn jiàn shuǐ jiù bù kěn zǒu
examples.en: The moment this child sees water, he refuses to leave.

drills.q: 他____听到这个数字就皱起了眉头。
drills.explain: 一 before the first verb plus 就 before the second is the frame for an immediate reaction. 也 would need a parallel clause or 无论……都……, 再 marks repetition or a future 'again', and 又 marks a repeated past action — none of them pairs with 就 to express immediacy.

drills.q: 他一听到这个消息，____坐不住了。
drills.explain: 一 in the first clause is answered by 就 in the second. 才 belongs with 只有 or 除非 and would reverse the relation; 还 marks continuation or 'still' and does not fit a single reaction; 再 marks repetition or a future 'again'.

reading.title: 别让铃声打断睡眠
reading.text:
我以前的闹钟声音很大，放在枕头旁边，每天早上都像被推了一把。铃声一响，我立刻就坐起来，人还没醒，心已经开始快跳。

后来我发现，这样醒来的头两个小时，几乎没法思考。开会时能听见别人说话，却常常记不住内容。一位研究睡眠的朋友说，这不是懒，是身体还没有准备好。

人从睡着到清醒需要一个过渡。早上被突然叫醒，大脑还停在浅睡状态，呼吸和心跳都没调整过来，情绪自然容易低落。光线比铃声柔和得多，也更容易让身体慢慢醒过来。这些危害看着不大，累起来却并不小。

现在我换了个办法：晚上把窗帘留一条缝，早上让光线进来；闹钟改成很轻的音乐，时间往后放十分钟。我做了个实验，坚持三个星期，起不来的次数少了很多。睡眠有它自己的规律，我们能做的，是尽量不去打断它。
reading.translation:
My old alarm clock was very loud and sat right by the pillow, so every morning felt like being shoved. The moment the bell rang I sat up at once — my body still asleep, my heart already racing.

Later I noticed that for the first two hours after waking that way I could barely think. In meetings I could hear other people talking but often could not remember what they said. A friend who studies sleep told me it was not laziness; the body simply was not ready.

Going from asleep to awake takes a transition. Woken abruptly in the morning, the brain is still in light sleep, breathing and heartbeat have not adjusted, and the mood drops easily. Light is far gentler than a bell, and it brings the body round more easily. These harms look small, but added up day after day they are not small at all.

So I changed two things: at night I leave a gap in the curtains so that light comes in in the morning, and the alarm is now very soft music set ten minutes later. I ran a small experiment for three weeks, and the number of mornings I could not get up dropped a lot. Sleep has its own regular pattern; what we can do is try not to interrupt it.

options: 现代人应该完全不用闹钟
被突然叫醒会影响早上的状态
音乐比光线更让人清醒
早起的人身体一定更好
questions.explain: The second and third paragraphs describe the foggy mornings and the transition the body needs, and the last paragraph offers a gentler way to wake — the harm of abrupt waking is the subject.

questions.q: 作者现在早上靠____醒过来。
options: 窗帘透进来的光线和轻音乐
questions.explain: The last paragraph lists both changes: 窗帘留一条缝，让光线进来 and 闹钟改成很轻的音乐.

questions.q: 从文章看，作者对睡眠规律的态度是____。
options: 应该顺着身体自己的规律
应该多做实验改造习惯
应该每天晚起一个小时
questions.explain: The closing line — 我们能做的，是尽量不去打断它 — shows acceptance of the body's own rhythm rather than a fight against it.

dictation: 我的闹钟声音太大，每天早上都被吓醒。
拉开窗帘，让光线进来，人会清醒得快一些。
快走几步，呼吸会变得深一点。
他的情绪不好，可能跟最近睡得太少有关。
生活有规律，身体的状态才会稳定。

writing.prompt: Describe your own morning routine and one change you made to it. Was it worth the trouble? Write for a colleague who keeps hitting snooze. Use the words below.
writing.model: 我以前的闹钟放在枕头边上，声音很响。每天早上一响，我就跳起来，可是人并不清醒，情绪也很差，到了下午才慢慢好起来。后来我做了两个改变：把闹钟换成轻一点的声音，晚上固定时间关灯。开始时很难，坚持三周以后，早上醒得比闹钟还早。规律的生活看起来慢，其实省下了很多力气。
writing.tips: Set the old routine first, then the change and how long it took to work. End with a plain sentence on what you gained, not a lecture.
